blurb: A Branch mounted in a Sandbox. The handle is sandbox:name, and the name defaults to the Branch: tests:agent.
reasons: Why exec is two fields: an agent needs the exit code and the output. Everything else (the exec id, byte counts, how it is stopped) is in the long form.
Why the CLI exits with the command's code: a shell script can write layerfs workspace exec tests:agent "npm test" && … and it works. The result JSON is still on stdout; a refusal exits 125.
Why long output is a tail and a file: the end of a build log is the part that says what failed. The whole stream is kept in a file, so nothing is capped and nothing is lost.
Why status lists paths: the question before a Commit is which files changed. A count answers nothing an agent can act on. The read is bounded, so the answer says when there is more than it saw.
Why cancel needs no exec id: the caller that wants a Workspace quiet rarely holds the id; --exec stays for ending one command of several.
Why the handle has no path form: every Workspace has a name, so one spelling names it everywhere.

calls.note: the handle of every mounted Workspace, to find one again. It reads Workspace records and asks no daemon: the home's own for a Sandbox on native or one reached directly, and one request to each other ready machine's worker for the records it keeps. A Sandbox whose machine is stopped, or whose worker did not answer, has no rows; it is named in not_listed as {sandbox, blocked_by | reason, message} (reason is timeout, busy or lost). Rows carry no state: workspace status and sandbox get ask the daemon. Ordered by Sandbox, then name

calls.new_work: The call is new. The home's Workspace records (`workspace/<id>.json`: name, branch, path, created) cover a Sandbox on `native` and one reached directly; for every other Sandbox the machine's worker keeps them, and a new worker request must list the records of the named Sandboxes (today a worker lists Workspaces only by asking one Sandbox's daemon). One request per ready machine in the page; a machine that is not ready is not contacted. Every Workspace needs a name for its handle: the default name is new work of `workspace.mount`. `not_listed` entries are {sandbox, blocked_by | reason, message}; the long form carries both keys, one of them null.

calls.note: answers the handle every Workspace call takes, sandbox:name, and the directory the daemon mounted it at. The default name is the Branch's name made valid: lowercased, with each character outside the Workspace name alphabet replaced by - (Feature/Login mounts as feature-login). A name in use is refused Exists with a fix naming --name, so a second mount of the same Branch needs --name. There is no --path: the daemon assigns the directory (/workspaces/<n> in the Sandbox; a folder under its run folder on macOS native). main is refused InvalidInput with a fix naming branch fork; a seventeenth Workspace is Capacity. commit is the Commit the Workspace stands on
calls.help: mount a Branch in a Sandbox

options.name: name
options.help: the Workspace's name within its Sandbox (1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit); default: the Branch's name made valid: lowercased, each character outside the Workspace name alphabet (lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `-`) replaced by `-`

calls.new_work: The default name is new: today a mount without `name` has none and its handle is `<sandbox>:<path>`. With the default, every handle is `<sandbox>:<name>` and the path form of the handle goes (the parser accepts both today). The default is the Branch's name made valid: lowercased, each character outside the Workspace name alphabet replaced by `-`. The code's name rule also wants 1 to 63 characters, a letter or digit at both ends and no reserved name, which that mapping alone does not give: the result is cut to 63 characters and `_`, `.` and `-` are trimmed from its ends, and a Branch whose default is then empty or reserved is refused `InvalidInput` with a `fix` naming `--name`. A default that is in use is refused `Exists` with a `fix` naming `--name`. Renames: `ws` to `workspace`, the 64-hex `workspace` to `id`, `base` to `commit`, `kind: Mounted` to `outcome: mounted`. `sandbox`, `container`, `image`, `platform`, `runtime` and `name` leave the answer (`sandbox get` answers the Sandbox's facts; the name is in the handle).

refusals.when: a Workspace of that name is mounted in the Sandbox
the Branch is main, or the default name is empty or reserved

calls.note: runs one bash command in the Workspace's directory and waits for it. Short: exit_code, and stdout and stderr only when not empty. A stream of at most 1 MiB is answered whole; a longer one answers its last 1 MiB and names the file that holds all of it (stdout_file, stderr_file: a path sandbox files reads, kept until the Workspace is unmounted). No total is capped. The shell exits with the command's own code and prints the result JSON on stdout; a refusal exits 125. A cancelled command answers cancelled:true and exit code 128 plus the signal. --cwd is a folder of the Workspace, as a path from its root; --env K=V repeats, and Node and Python pass one object; --stdin gives the command the caller's stdin, read whole before it starts (without it the command reads /dev/null); --stream writes the command's output to the caller's stdout and stderr and prints no result (Node and Python: the stdout and stderr functions), after the command ends, as today. --progress sends one event before the command starts, {"phase":"start","done":0,"total":1,"exec":"exec-…"}: the id workspace cancel --exec takes. There is no timeout. A lost reply is the refusal Unknown, which carries exec and a fix naming workspace cancel --exec; the command is never run again. The shell's --events is gone

calls.new_work: `--cwd`, `--env` and `--stdin` are new. The backend's request has the fields (`environment`, `directory`, `stdin`), but the control layer always sends `HOME` only, the mount directory and `stdin: false`; both backends refuse `stdin: true` (a command reads `/dev/null`); and the frame to a machine's worker carries a directory and no environment or stdin. Feeding stdin is new in both backends. Output files are new: today a stream over the 1 MiB inline window goes only to a sink (`--stream`, the `stdout`/`stderr` functions) through an unlinked spool file and is otherwise not kept, and the reply has that stream null with `streamed: true`. The spool must become a named file beside the Sandbox's daemon log that `sandbox files` reads and unmount deletes, and the reply must carry the stream's last 1 MiB. `stdout_bytes` and `stderr_bytes` in every long answer, `duration_ms` and `cancelled` as a key (`kind: cancelled` today) are new. The shell exits with the command's code in every form (only with `--stream` today). The progress event's shape is new (`{exec: {id}}` today). The `Unknown` refusal carrying `exec` is new: the id must be known to the caller's side before the command starts (it is today's first progress event). `kind`, `truncated` and `message` leave the answer; `exec_id` becomes `exec`. Output that is not UTF-8 stays bytes, as today.

refusals.when: the reply was lost: the command may have started and may still run; nothing is run again

calls.note: was workspace.exec_cancel. Ends every command running in the Workspace, or the one --exec names: SIGTERM to everything it started, then SIGKILL after 5 s. Three short forms. {"signal":"SIGTERM"}: a command was signalled and has ended; signal is the last one sent. {"already_ended":true}: nothing was running (the named command had finished, or has no record). {"unknown":true}: the machine's worker was not reached or did not answer, so nothing is known to have changed; cancel again once it answers. With several commands signal and unknown can stand together, and the long form's commands says which. All three exit 0. The cancelled command's own exec answers cancelled:true

options.help: end only this command: the exec id from its progress event, `sandbox get` or the long form; default: every running command

calls.new_work: Cancelling without an exec id is new on the call: the code that ends every live command of a Workspace exists (forced unmount and forced Sandbox removal use it) but no call reaches it. `outcome` is `cancelled`, `already_ended` (`ended` today) or `unknown`; with several commands it is the worst of `commands[].outcome` (unknown, then cancelled, then already_ended). The short keys replace today's `{outcome, signal}`. `commands` is new.

calls.note: commits everything changed in the Workspace since its base, whichever process changed it. commit is the Branch's new head. When the Branch moved since the mount the changes are merged first (merged:true; overwritten lists the paths a newer-write-wins rule decided, the first 20, then overwritten_count); --force commits over the moved head instead, and the long form's displaced is the head it replaced. Nothing to commit answers the head with unchanged:true. A conflict is the refusal Conflict, which names the head as commit and lists conflicts; --expected refuses the same way before anything is merged. The Workspace stays mounted

calls.new_work: `--expected` is new: today the call has no head guard; it merges when the Branch moved and is refused `Conflict` only when a path conflicts. Renames on what the call answers today: `head` to `commit`, `kind: UpToDate` to `unchanged: true`, `merged {from, head}` to `merged: true` with `merged_from` (the head merged in), `lww` to `overwritten` (paths) with `lww_truncated` as `overwritten_count`, `displaced_head` to `displaced`, the Commit's `time` to `created_at`. The Commit's other facts (`second_parent`, `base`, `via`, `logical`, the new-bytes counts) are `commit get`'s. The `Conflict` refusal carries `commit` (the head), `conflicts` (paths, the first 20) and `conflicts_count` (`detail.head`, `detail.conflicts`, `detail.conflicts_truncated` today).

refusals.when: a path conflicts, or the head is not --expected; nothing is committed

calls.note: ends the Workspace and deletes its overlay; the Branch's history stays. Refused Dirty while it has uncommitted changes (the refusal lists the paths as changes, with a fix naming workspace commit); --discard drops them. Refused Busy while a command runs (it lists the exec ids as running); --force cancels each one first and aborts the Workspace's connection, and a cancel that is not confirmed refuses it Unknown

calls.new_work: No new capability. `outcome` is `unmounted` or `force_unmounted` (`kind` today); `abort`, `detach` and `cleanup` are a forced unmount's three steps as it answers them today, lowercase, and null otherwise. The `Dirty` refusal carries `changes` (the first 20 entries, as `workspace status` lists them), `changes_count` and `pending_merge` (`detail.changed`, `detail.truncated` today); the `Busy` refusal carries `running` (`detail.execs` today).

refusals.when: --force, and a command's cancel was not confirmed

calls.note: what a Commit would capture now, from one bounded read of the overlay (the daemon's existing bound of 256 rows). changes is the first 20 entries read, each a path with its change (added, modified, removed); changes_count is the number of entries read and is given when it is more than the 20 shown; partial:true when the bound was hit, so there are more. An entry is not a file count: a renamed or removed folder is one entry, the folder's path with type: "dir" (type is left out for a file). --path narrows the answer to one folder, within the same bound. A clean Workspace answers {"changes":[]}. branch_moved:true when the Branch gained Commits since the mount (a Commit will merge). state is left out when ready: busy with its op while it mounts, commits or unmounts, broken with a fix after a failure. On a machine that is not ready the call is refused Unavailable with a fix naming machine start; it starts no machine

calls.new_work: The path list is new: today the call answers counts only (`overlay {inodes, entries, pending_merge}`). The daemon already reads changed paths for the `Dirty` refusal: at most 256 overlay rows, in path order, with no change kind. New in the daemon and on the worker frame: a status request that answers those entries with each one's `change` and `type`, the number read, whether the bound was hit, and a `--path` filter applied within the same read. The bound stays 256 rows; a folder renamed or removed is one row. `state` is new, from `activity` as in `sandbox.get`; `activity` stays in the long form as the daemon's own word (`idle`, `attaching`, `committing`, `closing`, `uncertain`, `local_failure`). Renames: `base` to `commit`, `head_moved_since_mount` to `branch_moved`, `overlay.inodes` and `overlay.entries` to `inode_count` and `entry_count`, `overlay.pending_merge` to `pending_merge`; `kind` leaves the answer.
